blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

#!/bin/bash
# Mirrors .github/workflows/quality.yml crap job:
#   nyc instrument → node harness with coverage → crap4js ratchet vs released baseline.
# crap4js runs against the ORIGINAL tree (coverage keys carry the original absolute paths;

set -u
REPO=/home/runner/work/dmtools-agents/dmtools-agents
BIN=/tmp/tools/node_modules/.bin
WORK=/tmp/crapwork
cd "$REPO"
rm -rf "$WORK"
mkdir -p "$WORK"
"$BIN/nyc" instrument --cwd . . "$WORK/inst" 2>/dev/null
rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$WORK/inst/"
(cd "$WORK/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)
FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"

HC=$?

tail -2 "$WORK/harness.log"
CRAP="$BIN/crap4js"
"$CRAP" . --coverage "$WORK/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 8 --baseline /tmp/base/crap-baseline.json > "$WORK/crap.txt"
RC=$?
echo "crap4js exit=$RC"

#!/bin/bash

#!/bin/bash

4. `-m` at END of args (no next) → skip

6. `-mMsg` joined → inline substring(2)

Also '--message' exact → first branch (next token). Note: '--message' also... first condition `a === '-m' || a === '--message' || /^-[a-zA-Z]*m$/.test(a)`.

```js
/**
 * The message value carried by an -m/--message-style flag at args[i] —
 * the following token, or null when the flag is the last argument.
 */
function messageValueAfter(args, i) {
   return i + 1 < args.length ? args[i + 1] : null;  // CC 2
}

/**

 * files; this module stays I/O-free) — null when unknown/empty.
 */
function fileContentFor(fileContents, path) {
   return (fileContents && fileContents[path]) ? fileContents[path] : null; // CC 3 (&& + ternary)
}
``

Wait original: `if (i + 1 < args.length && fileContents && fileContents[args[i + 1]]) parts.push(fileContents[args[i + 1]]);` — the i+1 bounds check is included. So fileFlagPart:

```js
function fileFlagPart(args, i, fileContents) {
   var content = i + 1 < args.length ? fileContentFor(fileContents, args[i + 1]) : null;
   return { text: content, next: i + 2 };  // CC: 1 + ternary 1 = 2
}
``

Crap counting: fileContentFor CC = ternary + && = 3. messageValueAfter CC 2.

isMessageValueFlag CC: `a === '-m' || a === '--message' || /^.../.test(a)` → CC 3.
isFileValueFlag CC 3.
isInlineMessageOption CC 1 (or 2 if I count `=== 0`... no decisions, CC 1).
isJoinedShortMessage: `a.indexOf('-m') === 0 && a.length > 2 && a.indexOf('--') !== 0` → CC 3.
isInlineFileOption CC 1.

commitMessagePartAt:

```js
function commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents) {
   var a = args[i];
   if (isMessageValueFlag(a)) {
       var value = messageValueAfter(args, i);
       return { text: value, next: value === null ? i + 1 : i + 2 };  // CC 1 + ternary 1

   if (isJoinedShortMessage(a)) return { text: a.substring(2), next: i + 1 };

   if (isInlineFileOption(a)) return { text: fileContentFor(fileContents, a.substring('--file='.length)), next: i + 1 };
   return { text: null, next: i + 1 };
}
``

commitMessageText:

```js
function commitMessageText(args, fileContents) {
   var parts = [];
   var i = 0;
   while (i < args.length) {
       var part = commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents);
       if (part.text !== null) parts.push(part.text);
       i = part.next;

}
``

CC: 1 + while + if = 3. ✓

1. `-m`/`--message`/cluster with next: push args[i+1] (even ''), i+=2. Mine: value = args[i+1] (could be ''), text!==null → push, next i+2. ✓

3. `--message=X`: push X, i+=1. Mine: text X (could be '' for '--message=') → push '' (original pushes '' too), next i+1. ✓
4. joined -mX: push substring(2), i+=1. ✓
5. -F with content: original `if (i+1 < len && fileContents && fileContents[next])` push, i+=2 unconditionally. Mine: fileFlagPart: content = in-bounds ? fileContentFor(...) : null; text pushed iff non-null; next always i+2. ✓

  - in-bounds + no content → nothing, i+=2 ✓
  - out of bounds (-F at end) → nothing, i+=2 → loop ends ✓
6. `--file=f`: original `if (fileContents && fileContents[f]) parts.push(...)`; i+=1. Mine: text = fileContentFor (null-safe), next i+1. ✓
7. other tokens: skip i+=1. ✓

One more subtlety — ORDER of checks. Original order: (1) -m cluster... (2) --message= (3) joined -m (4) -F cluster (5) --file=. Mine keeps the same order. ✓

Could a token match BOTH isMessageValueFlag and isInlineMessageOption? '-m...' variants: '--message=' — does it match cluster regex? '^-[a-zA-Z]*m$' — '--message=' has '=', no. ✓ disjoint enough.

#!/bin/bash
# Mirrors .github/workflows/quality.yml crap job:
#   nyc instrument → node harness with coverage → crap4js ratchet vs released baseline.
# crap4js runs against the ORIGINAL tree (coverage keys carry the original absolute paths;
# nyc instrumentation preserves line numbering).
set -u
REPO=/home/runner/work/dmtools-agents/dmtools-agents
BIN=/tmp/tools/node_modules/.bin
WORK=/tmp/crapwork
cd "$REPO"
rm -rf "$WORK"
mkdir -p "$WORK"
"$BIN/nyc" instrument --cwd . . "$WORK/inst" 2>/dev/null
rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$WORK/inst/"
(cd "$WORK/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)
FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
  "$WORK/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
  "$WORK/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES > "$WORK/harness.log" 2>&1
HC=$?
echo "harness exit=$HC"
tail -2 "$WORK/harness.log"
CRAP="$BIN/crap4js"
"$CRAP" . --coverage "$WORK/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 8 --baseline /tmp/base/crap-baseline.json > "$WORK/crap.txt"
RC=$?
echo "crap4js exit=$RC"
sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$WORK/crap.txt"
exit $RC
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/run_crap.sh
# count functions above 8 + max CRAP from the full report (all functions listed?)
grep -cE "^\S+\s+\S+\s+[0-9.]+\s+" /tmp/crap_orig.txt; grep -P "^\S+\s+\S+\s+[0-9.]+\s+[0-9.]+%\s+[0-9.]+$" /tmp/crap_orig.txt | awk '{print $NF}' | sort -rn | head -3"}

1. `-m msg` → next token
2. `--message msg` → next token
3. `-cm`-style cluster (regex `/^-[a-zA-Z]*m$/`) → next token
4. `-m` at END of args (no next) → skip
5. `--message=msg` → inline
6. `-mMsg` joined → inline substring(2)
7. `-F file` with map content → file content, skips value (i+=2)
8. `-F file` WITHOUT map content → nothing pushed, still skips (i+=2)
9. `-F` at end → skip (i+=2)
10. `--file=file` with map → content
11. `--file=file` without map → nothing
12. unrelated tokens skipped
13. multiple parts joined with '\n'
14. empty args → ''
15. `--file=` empty path → nothing (fileContents['] undefined)
16. cluster `-abcF` → file flag with next as file
17. `-m ''` (empty next token) → pushes ''

Also check: how do the current tests load the module? `loadModule('js/common/gitPushGuard.js', makeRequire({}), {})` — and file_read global available (shim parity suite uses file_read directly — provided by the harness's global env? The test uses `file_read({path})` — the node harness provides file_* globals presumably).

Now the `-F` branch: `if (a === '-F' || a === '--file' || /^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/.test(a))`. NOTE: the regex `/^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/` also matches '--file'? No: '--file' = '-','file'... wait /^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/ — '--file' has chars - f i l e: after first '-', the rest '-file' contains '-', not in [a-zA-Z], so no match. OK.

Important subtlety: `-m` branch FIRST: `/^-[a-zA-Z]*m$/` matches '-m'... and ALSO '-mF'? No wait: '-mF' ends with F — cluster-m regex needs to END with m: '-mF' doesn't match. Cluster-F regex /^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/ matches '-mF'! So '-mF file.txt' → treated as -F cluster flag. Fun. I'll include that in tests.

Also '--message' exact → first branch (next token). Note: '--message' also... first condition `a === '-m' || a === '--message' || /^-[a-zA-Z]*m$/.test(a)`.

What about '-m' cluster regex matching '--'? No ('-' not in class).

Edge: '-mx' — cluster-m fails (ends x), --message= fails, joined: indexOf('-m')===0 ✓, length 3>2 ✓, indexOf('--')!==0 ✓ → pushed 'x'.

Edge: '--mx'? indexOf('-m') — '--mx'.indexOf('-m') = 1 ≠ 0 → not joined. Skipped entirely.

Edge: '-m=' — joined: substring(2) = '='.

Now the empty-string value edge: `['-m', ']` → parts.push(') → join('\n') = ''. Characterization: commitMessageText(['-m',']) === ''.

And what does commitMessageText([], ...) return? '' (join of empty). And commitMessageText(undefined)? `args.length` would throw — callers always pass arrays (extractSubcommand guarantees args: []). Not my concern; keep as is.

Now for `fileContents` truthiness: `{}` → fileContents truthy but lookup undefined → skip.

Careful design of the extraction to keep CRAP ≤ 8 per helper with 100% coverage:

```js
/**
 * The message value carried by an -m/--message-style flag at args[i] —
 * the following token, or null when the flag is the last argument.
 */
function messageValueAfter(args, i) {
   return i + 1 < args.length ? args[i + 1] : null;  // CC 2
}

/**
 * File content registered for a -F/--file argument path (the caller reads
 * files; this module stays I/O-free) — null when unknown/empty.
 */
function fileContentFor(fileContents, path) {
   return (fileContents && fileContents[path]) ? fileContents[path] : null; // CC 3 (&& + ternary)
}
``

Wait original: `if (i + 1 < args.length && fileContents && fileContents[args[i + 1]]) parts.push(fileContents[args[i + 1]]);` — the i+1 bounds check is included. So fileFlagPart:

```js
function fileFlagPart(args, i, fileContents) {
   var content = i + 1 < args.length ? fileContentFor(fileContents, args[i + 1]) : null;
   return { text: content, next: i + 2 };  // CC: 1 + ternary 1 = 2
}
``

Crap counting: fileContentFor CC = ternary + && = 3. messageValueAfter CC 2.

isMessageValueFlag CC: `a === '-m' || a === '--message' || /^.../.test(a)` → CC 3.
isFileValueFlag CC 3.
isInlineMessageOption CC 1 (or 2 if I count `=== 0`... no decisions, CC 1).
isJoinedShortMessage: `a.indexOf('-m') === 0 && a.length > 2 && a.indexOf('--') !== 0` → CC 3.
isInlineFileOption CC 1.

commitMessagePartAt:

```js
function commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents) {
   var a = args[i];
   if (isMessageValueFlag(a)) {
       var value = messageValueAfter(args, i);
       return { text: value, next: value === null ? i + 1 : i + 2 };  // CC 1 + ternary 1
   }
   if (isInlineMessageOption(a)) return { text: a.substring('--message='.length), next: i + 1 };
   if (isJoinedShortMessage(a)) return { text: a.substring(2), next: i + 1 };
   if (isFileValueFlag(a)) return fileFlagPart(args, i, fileContents);
   if (isInlineFileOption(a)) return { text: fileContentFor(fileContents, a.substring('--file='.length)), next: i + 1 };
   return { text: null, next: i + 1 };
}
``

CC: 1 + 5 ifs + 1 ternary = 7. Under 8 ✓ (needs 100% coverage: each if both ways — my characterization matrix covers every one: message flag (yes via -m; no via others), inline message (yes --message=), joined (-mx), file flag (-F), inline file (--file=), default (token 'x')).

commitMessageText:

```js
function commitMessageText(args, fileContents) {
   var parts = [];
   var i = 0;
   while (i < args.length) {
       var part = commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents);
       if (part.text !== null) parts.push(part.text);
       i = part.next;
   }
   return parts.join('\n');
}
``

CC: 1 + while + if = 3. ✓

Equivalence audit vs original, case by case:
1. `-m`/`--message`/cluster with next: push args[i+1] (even ''), i+=2. Mine: value = args[i+1] (could be ''), text!==null → push, next i+2. ✓
2. message flag at end (no next): original pushes nothing, i+=1. Mine: value null → text null → no push, next i+1. ✓
3. `--message=X`: push X, i+=1. Mine: text X (could be '' for '--message=') → push '' (original pushes '' too), next i+1. ✓
4. joined -mX: push substring(2), i+=1. ✓
5. -F with content: original `if (i+1 < len && fileContents && fileContents[next])` push, i+=2 unconditionally. Mine: fileFlagPart: content = in-bounds ? fileContentFor(...) : null; text pushed iff non-null; next always i+2. ✓ 
  - in-bounds + content → push content, i+=2 ✓
  - in-bounds + no content → nothing, i+=2 ✓
  - out of bounds (-F at end) → nothing, i+=2 → loop ends ✓
6. `--file=f`: original `if (fileContents && fileContents[f]) parts.push(...)`; i+=1. Mine: text = fileContentFor (null-safe), next i+1. ✓
7. other tokens: skip i+=1. ✓

One more subtlety — ORDER of checks. Original order: (1) -m cluster... (2) --message= (3) joined -m (4) -F cluster (5) --file=. Mine keeps the same order. ✓

Could a token match BOTH isMessageValueFlag and isInlineMessageOption? '-m...' variants: '--message=' — does it match cluster regex? '^-[a-zA-Z]*m$' — '--message=' has '=', no. ✓ disjoint enough.

Now — gitPushGuard exports: add commitMessagePartAt? The existing exports list all helpers. I'll export: isMessageValueFlag? #!/bin/bash
# Mirrors .github/workflows/quality.yml crap job:
#   nyc instrument → node harness with coverage → crap4js ratchet vs released baseline.
# crap4js runs against the ORIGINAL tree (coverage keys carry the original absolute paths;

set -u
REPO=/home/runner/work/dmtools-agents/dmtools-agents
BIN=/tmp/tools/node_modules/.bin
WORK=/tmp/crapwork
cd "$REPO"
rm -rf "$WORK"
mkdir -p "$WORK"
"$BIN/nyc" instrument --cwd . . "$WORK/inst" 2>/dev/null
rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$WORK/inst/"
(cd "$WORK/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)
FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"

HC=$?

tail -2 "$WORK/harness.log"
CRAP="$BIN/crap4js"
"$CRAP" . --coverage "$WORK/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 8 --baseline /tmp/base/crap-baseline.json > "$WORK/crap.txt"
RC=$?
echo "crap4js exit=$RC"

I have the full picture of test_gitPushGuard.js. The `commitMessageText` function is only exercised indirectly through `evaluateCommit`. I need to add direct characterization tests covering ALL branches of commitMessageText:

1. `-m msg` → next token
2. `--message msg` → next token
3. `-cm`-style cluster (regex `/^-[a-zA-Z]*m$/`) → next token
4. `-m` at END of args (no next) → skip
5. `--message=msg` → inline
6. `-mMsg` joined → inline substring(2)
7. `-F file` with map content → file content, skips value (i+=2)
8. `-F file` WITHOUT map content → nothing pushed, still skips (i+=2)
9. `-F` at end → skip (i+=2)
10. `--file=file` with map → content
11. `--file=file` without map → nothing
12. unrelated tokens skipped
13. multiple parts joined with '\n'
14. empty args → ''
15. `--file=` empty path → nothing (fileContents['] undefined)
16. cluster `-abcF` → file flag with next as file
17. `-m ''` (empty next token) → pushes ''

Also check: how do the current tests load the module? `loadModule('js/common/gitPushGuard.js', makeRequire({}), {})` — and file_read global available (shim parity suite uses file_read directly — provided by the harness's global env? The test uses `file_read({path})` — the node harness provides file_* globals presumably).

Now the `-F` branch: `if (a === '-F' || a === '--file' || /^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/.test(a))`. NOTE: the regex `/^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/` also matches '--file'? No: '--file' = '-','file'... wait /^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/ — '--file' has chars - f i l e: after first '-', the rest '-file' contains '-', not in [a-zA-Z], so no match. OK.

Important subtlety: `-m` branch FIRST: `/^-[a-zA-Z]*m$/` matches '-m'... and ALSO '-mF'? No wait: '-mF' ends with F — cluster-m regex needs to END with m: '-mF' doesn't match. Cluster-F regex /^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/ matches '-mF'! So '-mF file.txt' → treated as -F cluster flag. Fun. I'll include that in tests.

Also '--message' exact → first branch (next token). Note: '--message' also... first condition `a === '-m' || a === '--message' || /^-[a-zA-Z]*m$/.test(a)`.

What about '-m' cluster regex matching '--'? No ('-' not in class).

Edge: '-mx' — cluster-m fails (ends x), --message= fails, joined: indexOf('-m')===0 ✓, length 3>2 ✓, indexOf('--')!==0 ✓ → pushed 'x'.

Edge: '--mx'? indexOf('-m') — '--mx'.indexOf('-m') = 1 ≠ 0 → not joined. Skipped entirely.

Edge: '-m=' — joined: substring(2) = '='.

Now the empty-string value edge: `['-m', ']` → parts.push(') → join('\n') = ''. Characterization: commitMessageText(['-m',']) === ''.

And what does commitMessageText([], ...) return? '' (join of empty). And commitMessageText(undefined)? `args.length` would throw — callers always pass arrays (extractSubcommand guarantees args: []). Not my concern; keep as is.

Now for `fileContents` truthiness: `{}` → fileContents truthy but lookup undefined → skip.

Careful design of the extraction to keep CRAP ≤ 8 per helper with 100% coverage:

```js
/**
 * The message value carried by an -m/--message-style flag at args[i] —
 * the following token, or null when the flag is the last argument.
 */
function messageValueAfter(args, i) {
   return i + 1 < args.length ? args[i + 1] : null;  // CC 2
}

/**
 * File content registered for a -F/--file argument path (the caller reads
 * files; this module stays I/O-free) — null when unknown/empty.
 */
function fileContentFor(fileContents, path) {
   return (fileContents && fileContents[path]) ? fileContents[path] : null; // CC 3 (&& + ternary)
}
``

Wait original: `if (i + 1 < args.length && fileContents && fileContents[args[i + 1]]) parts.push(fileContents[args[i + 1]]);` — the i+1 bounds check is included. So fileFlagPart:

```js
function fileFlagPart(args, i, fileContents) {
   var content = i + 1 < args.length ? fileContentFor(fileContents, args[i + 1]) : null;
   return { text: content, next: i + 2 };  // CC: 1 + ternary 1 = 2
}
``

Crap counting: fileContentFor CC = ternary + && = 3. messageValueAfter CC 2.

isMessageValueFlag CC: `a === '-m' || a === '--message' || /^.../.test(a)` → CC 3.
isFileValueFlag CC 3.
isInlineMessageOption CC 1 (or 2 if I count `=== 0`... no decisions, CC 1).
isJoinedShortMessage: `a.indexOf('-m') === 0 && a.length > 2 && a.indexOf('--') !== 0` → CC 3.
isInlineFileOption CC 1.

commitMessagePartAt:

```js
function commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents) {
   var a = args[i];
   if (isMessageValueFlag(a)) {
       var value = messageValueAfter(args, i);
       return { text: value, next: value === null ? i + 1 : i + 2 };  // CC 1 + ternary 1
   }
   if (isInlineMessageOption(a)) return { text: a.substring('--message='.length), next: i + 1 };
   if (isJoinedShortMessage(a)) return { text: a.substring(2), next: i + 1 };
   if (isFileValueFlag(a)) return fileFlagPart(args, i, fileContents);
   if (isInlineFileOption(a)) return { text: fileContentFor(fileContents, a.substring('--file='.length)), next: i + 1 };
   return { text: null, next: i + 1 };
}
``

CC: 1 + 5 ifs + 1 ternary = 7. Under 8 ✓ (needs 100% coverage: each if both ways — my characterization matrix covers every one: message flag (yes via -m; no via others), inline message (yes --message=), joined (-mx), file flag (-F), inline file (--file=), default (token 'x')).

commitMessageText:

```js
function commitMessageText(args, fileContents) {
   var parts = [];
   var i = 0;
   while (i < args.length) {
       var part = commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents);
       if (part.text !== null) parts.push(part.text);
       i = part.next;
   }
   return parts.join('\n');
}
``

CC: 1 + while + if = 3. ✓

Equivalence audit vs original, case by case:
1. `-m`/`--message`/cluster with next: push args[i+1] (even ''), i+=2. Mine: value = args[i+1] (could be ''), text!==null → push, next i+2. ✓
2. message flag at end (no next): original pushes nothing, i+=1. Mine: value null → text null → no push, next i+1. ✓
3. `--message=X`: push X, i+=1. Mine: text X (could be '' for '--message=') → push '' (original pushes '' too), next i+1. ✓
4. joined -mX: push substring(2), i+=1. ✓
5. -F with content: original `if (i+1 < len && fileContents && fileContents[next])` push, i+=2 unconditionally. Mine: fileFlagPart: content = in-bounds ? fileContentFor(...) : null; text pushed iff non-null; next always i+2. ✓ 
  - in-bounds + content → push content, i+=2 ✓
  - in-bounds + no content → nothing, i+=2 ✓
  - out of bounds (-F at end) → nothing, i+=2 → loop ends ✓
6. `--file=f`: original `if (fileContents && fileContents[f]) parts.push(...)`; i+=1. Mine: text = fileContentFor (null-safe), next i+1. ✓
7. other tokens: skip i+=1. ✓

One more subtlety — ORDER of checks. Original order: (1) -m cluster... (2) --message= (3) joined -m (4) -F cluster (5) --file=. Mine keeps the same order. ✓

Could a token match BOTH isMessageValueFlag and isInlineMessageOption? '-m...' variants: '--message=' — does it match cluster regex? '^-[a-zA-Z]*m$' — '--message=' has '=', no. ✓ disjoint enough.

Now — gitPushGuard exports: add commitMessagePartAt? The existing exports list all helpers. I'll export: isMessageValueFlag? Hmm — exporting every tiny predicate is noise; but for CRAP ≤ 8 each needs full coverage, which the characterization matrix gives INDIRECTLY through commitMessageText (coverage counts per line/function). crap4js computes per-function coverage from statements intersecting the method's line range — indirect coverage through commitMessageText's tests covers the helpers' statements as long as the helper code is EXECUTED. isMessageValueFlag true/false both covered by the matrix. So I don't strictly need direct tests of predicates, but a few direct assertions are cheap and pin each helper. I'll export the new helpers and add a handful of direct tests (plus the full matrix through commitMessageText + evaluateCommit).

I have the full picture of test_gitPushGuard.js. The `commitMessageText` function is only exercised indirectly through `evaluateCommit`. I need to add direct characterization tests covering ALL branches of commitMessageText:

1. `-m msg` → next token
2. `--message msg` → next token
3. `-cm`-style cluster (regex `/^-[a-zA-Z]*m$/`) → next token
4. `-m` at END of args (no next) → skip
5. `--message=msg` → inline
6. `-mMsg` joined → inline substring(2)
7. `-F file` with map content → file content, skips value (i+=2)
8. `-F file` WITHOUT map content → nothing pushed, still skips (i+=2)
9. `-F` at end → skip (i+=2)
10. `--file=file` with map → content
11. `--file=file` without map → nothing
12. unrelated tokens skipped
13. multiple parts joined with '\n'
14. empty args → ''
15. `--file=` empty path → nothing (fileContents['] undefined)
16. cluster `-abcF` → file flag with next as file
17. `-m ''` (empty next token) → pushes ''

Also check: how do the current tests load the module? `loadModule('js/common/gitPushGuard.js', makeRequire({}), {})` — and file_read global available (shim parity suite uses file_read directly — provided by the harness's global env? The test uses `file_read({path})` — the node harness provides file_* globals presumably).

Now the `-F` branch: `if (a === '-F' || a === '--file' || /^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/.test(a))`. NOTE: the regex `/^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/` also matches '--file'? No: '--file' = '-','file'... wait /^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/ — '--file' has chars - f i l e: after first '-', the rest '-file' contains '-', not in [a-zA-Z], so no match. OK.

Important subtlety: `-m` branch FIRST: `/^-[a-zA-Z]*m$/` matches '-m'... and ALSO '-mF'? No wait: '-mF' ends with F — cluster-m regex needs to END with m: '-mF' doesn't match. Cluster-F regex /^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/ matches '-mF'! So '-mF file.txt' → treated as -F cluster flag. Fun. I'll include that in tests.

Also '--message' exact → first branch (next token). Note: '--message' also... first condition `a === '-m' || a === '--message' || /^-[a-zA-Z]*m$/.test(a)`.

What about '-m' cluster regex matching '--'? No ('-' not in class).

Edge: '-mx' — cluster-m fails (ends x), --message= fails, joined: indexOf('-m')===0 ✓, length 3>2 ✓, indexOf('--')!==0 ✓ → pushed 'x'.

Edge: '--mx'? indexOf('-m') — '--mx'.indexOf('-m') = 1 ≠ 0 → not joined. Skipped entirely.

Edge: '-m=' — joined: substring(2) = '='.

Now the empty-string value edge: `['-m', ']` → parts.push(') → join('\n') = ''. Characterization: commitMessageText(['-m',']) === ''.

And what does commitMessageText([], ...) return? '' (join of empty). And commitMessageText(undefined)? `args.length` would throw — callers always pass arrays (extractSubcommand guarantees args: []). Not my concern; keep as is.

Now for `fileContents` truthiness: `{}` → fileContents truthy but lookup undefined → skip.

Careful design of the extraction to keep CRAP ≤ 8 per helper with 100% coverage:

```js
/**
 * The message value carried by an -m/--message-style flag at args[i] —
 * the following token, or null when the flag is the last argument.
 */
function messageValueAfter(args, i) {
   return i + 1 < args.length ? args[i + 1] : null;  // CC 2
}

/**
 * File content registered for a -F/--file argument path (the caller reads
 * files; this module stays I/O-free) — null when unknown/empty.
 */
function fileContentFor(fileContents, path) {
   return (fileContents && fileContents[path]) ? fileContents[path] : null; // CC 3 (&& + ternary)
}
``

Wait original: `if (i + 1 < args.length && fileContents && fileContents[args[i + 1]]) parts.push(fileContents[args[i + 1]]);` — the i+1 bounds check is included. So fileFlagPart:

```js
function fileFlagPart(args, i, fileContents) {
   var content = i + 1 < args.length ? fileContentFor(fileContents, args[i + 1]) : null;
   return { text: content, next: i + 2 };  // CC: 1 + ternary 1 = 2
}
``

Crap counting: fileContentFor CC = ternary + && = 3. messageValueAfter CC 2.

isMessageValueFlag CC: `a === '-m' || a === '--message' || /^.../.test(a)` → CC 3.
isFileValueFlag CC 3.
isInlineMessageOption CC 1 (or 2 if I count `=== 0`... no decisions, CC 1).
isJoinedShortMessage: `a.indexOf('-m') === 0 && a.length > 2 && a.indexOf('--') !== 0` → CC 3.
isInlineFileOption CC 1.

commitMessagePartAt:

```js
function commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents) {
   var a = args[i];
   if (isMessageValueFlag(a)) {
       var value = messageValueAfter(args, i);
       return { text: value, next: value === null ? i + 1 : i + 2 };  // CC 1 + ternary 1
   }
   if (isInlineMessageOption(a)) return { text: a.substring('--message='.length), next: i + 1 };
   if (isJoinedShortMessage(a)) return { text: a.substring(2), next: i + 1 };
   if (isFileValueFlag(a)) return fileFlagPart(args, i, fileContents);
   if (isInlineFileOption(a)) return { text: fileContentFor(fileContents, a.substring('--file='.length)), next: i + 1 };
   return { text: null, next: i + 1 };
}
``

CC: 1 + 5 ifs + 1 ternary = 7. Under 8 ✓ (needs 100% coverage: each if both ways — my characterization matrix covers every one: message flag (yes via -m; no via others), inline message (yes --message=), joined (-mx), file flag (-F), inline file (--file=), default (token 'x')).

commitMessageText:

```js
function commitMessageText(args, fileContents) {
   var parts = [];
   var i = 0;
   while (i < args.length) {
       var part = commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents);
       if (part.text !== null) parts.push(part.text);
       i = part.next;
   }
   return parts.join('\n');
}
``

CC: 1 + while + if = 3. ✓

Equivalence audit vs original, case by case:
1. `-m`/`--message`/cluster with next: push args[i+1] (even ''), i+=2. Mine: value = args[i+1] (could be ''), text!==null → push, next i+2. ✓
2. message flag at end (no next): original pushes nothing, i+=1. Mine: value null → text null → no push, next i+1. ✓
3. `--message=X`: push X, i+=1. Mine: text X (could be '' for '--message=') → push '' (original pushes '' too), next i+1. ✓
4. joined -mX: push substring(2), i+=1. ✓
5. -F with content: original `if (i+1 < len && fileContents && fileContents[next])` push, i+=2 unconditionally. Mine: fileFlagPart: content = in-bounds ? fileContentFor(...) : null; text pushed iff non-null; next always i+2. ✓ 
  - in-bounds + content → push content, i+=2 ✓
  - in-bounds + no content → nothing, i+=2 ✓
  - out of bounds (-F at end) → nothing, i+=2 → loop ends ✓
6. `--file=f`: original `if (fileContents && fileContents[f]) parts.push(...)`; i+=1. Mine: text = fileContentFor (null-safe), next i+1. ✓
7. other tokens: skip i+=1. ✓

One more subtlety — ORDER of checks. Original order: (1) -m cluster... (2) --message= (3) joined -m (4) -F cluster (5) --file=. Mine keeps the same order. ✓

Could a token match BOTH isMessageValueFlag and isInlineMessageOption? '-m...' variants: '--message=' — does it match cluster regex? '^-[a-zA-Z]*m$' — '--message=' has '=', no. ✓ disjoint enough.

Now — gitPushGuard exports: add commitMessagePartAt? The existing exports list all helpers. I'll export: isMessageValueFlag? Hmm — exporting every tiny predicate is noise; but for CRAP ≤ 8 each needs full coverage, which the characterization matrix gives INDIRECTLY through commitMessageText (coverage counts per line/function). crap4js computes per-function coverage from statements intersecting the method's line range — indirect coverage through commitMessageText's tests covers the helpers' statements as long as the helper code is EXECUTED. isMessageValueFlag true/false both covered by the matrix. So I don't strictly need direct tests of predicates, but a few direct assertions are cheap and pin each helper. ```js
/**
 * The message value carried by an -m/--message-style flag at args[i] —
 * the following token, or null when the flag is the last argument.
 */
function messageValueAfter(args, i) {
   return i + 1 < args.length ? args[i + 1] : null;  // CC 2
}

/**
 * File content registered for a -F/--file argument path (the caller reads
 * files; this module stays I/O-free) — null when unknown/empty.

function fileContentFor(fileContents, path) {
   return (fileContents && fileContents[path]) ? fileContents[path] : null; // CC 3 (&& + ternary)
}
``

Wait original: `if (i + 1 < args.length && fileContents && fileContents[args[i + 1]]) parts.push(fileContents[args[i + 1]]);` — the i+1 bounds check is included. So fileFlagPart:

```js
function fileFlagPart(args, i, fileContents) {
   var content = i + 1 < args.length ? fileContentFor(fileContents, args[i + 1]) : null;
   return { text: content, next: i + 2 };  // CC: 1 + ternary 1 = 2
}
``

isMessageValueFlag CC: `a === '-m' || a === '--message' || /^.../.test(a)` → CC 3.
isFileValueFlag CC 3.
isInlineMessageOption CC 1 (or 2 if I count `=== 0`... no decisions, CC 1).
isJoinedShortMessage: `a.indexOf('-m') === 0 && a.length > 2 && a.indexOf('--') !== 0` → CC 3.
isInlineFileOption CC 1.

commitMessagePartAt:

```js
function commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents) {
   var a = args[i];
   if (isMessageValueFlag(a)) {
       var value = messageValueAfter(args, i);
       return { text: value, next: value === null ? i + 1 : i + 2 };  // CC 1 + ternary 1

   if (isJoinedShortMessage(a)) return { text: a.substring(2), next: i + 1 };
   if (isFileValueFlag(a)) return fileFlagPart(args, i, fileContents);
   if (isInlineFileOption(a)) return { text: fileContentFor(fileContents, a.substring('--file='.length)), next: i + 1 };
   return { text: null, next: i + 1 };
}
``

function commitMessageText(args, fileContents) {

}

#!/bin/bash

Important subtlety: `-m` branch FIRST: `/^-[a-zA-Z]*m$/` matches '-m'... and ALSO '-mF'? No wait: '-mF' ends with F — cluster-m regex needs to END with m: '-mF' doesn't match. Cluster-F regex /^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/ matches '-mF'! So '-mF file.txt' → treated as -F cluster flag. Fun. I'll include that in tests.

```js
/**
 * The message value carried by an -m/--message-style flag at args[i] —
 * the following token, or null when the flag is the last argument.
 */
function messageValueAfter(args, i) {
   return i + 1 < args.length ? args[i + 1] : null;  // CC 2
}

/**
 * File content registered for a -F/--file argument path (the caller reads
 * files; this module stays I/O-free) — null when unknown/empty.
 */
function fileContentFor(fileContents, path) {
   return (fileContents && fileContents[path]) ? fileContents[path] : null; // CC 3 (&& + ternary)
}
``

Wait original: `if (i + 1 < args.length && fileContents && fileContents[args[i + 1]]) parts.push(fileContents[args[i + 1]]);` — the i+1 bounds check is included. So fileFlagPart:

```js
function fileFlagPart(args, i, fileContents) {
   var content = i + 1 < args.length ? fileContentFor(fileContents, args[i + 1]) : null;
   return { text: content, next: i + 2 };  // CC: 1 + ternary 1 = 2
}
``

Crap counting: fileContentFor CC = ternary + && = 3. messageValueAfter CC 2.

isMessageValueFlag CC: `a === '-m' || a === '--message' || /^.../.test(a)` → CC 3.
isFileValueFlag CC 3.
isInlineMessageOption CC 1 (or 2 if I count `=== 0`... no decisions, CC 1).
isJoinedShortMessage: `a.indexOf('-m') === 0 && a.length > 2 && a.indexOf('--') !== 0` → CC 3.
isInlineFileOption CC 1.

commitMessagePartAt:

```js
function commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents) {
   var a = args[i];
   if (isMessageValueFlag(a)) {
       var value = messageValueAfter(args, i);
       return { text: value, next: value === null ? i + 1 : i + 2 };  // CC 1 + ternary 1

   if (isJoinedShortMessage(a)) return { text: a.substring(2), next: i + 1 };
   if (isFileValueFlag(a)) return fileFlagPart(args, i, fileContents);
   if (isInlineFileOption(a)) return { text: fileContentFor(fileContents, a.substring('--file='.length)), next: i + 1 };
   return { text: null, next: i + 1 };
}
``

CC: 1 + 5 ifs + 1 ternary = 7. Under 8 ✓ (needs 100% coverage: each if both ways — my characterization matrix covers every one: message flag (yes via -m; no via others), inline message (yes --message=), joined (-mx), file flag (-F), inline file (--file=), default (token 'x')).

commitMessageText:

```js
function commitMessageText(args, fileContents) {
   var parts = [];
   var i = 0;
   while (i < args.length) {
       var part = commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents);
       if (part.text !== null) parts.push(part.text);

}
``

CC: 1 + while + if = 3. ✓

1. `-m`/`--message`/cluster with next: push args[i+1] (even ''), i+=2. Mine: value = args[i+1] (could be ''), text!==null → push, next i+2. ✓

4. joined -mX: push substring(2), i+=1. ✓

7. other tokens: skip i+=1. ✓

```js
/**

 * the following token, or null when the flag is the last argument.
 */
function messageValueAfter(args, i) {

}

/**

}
``

```js
function commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents) {
   var a = args[i];
   if (isMessageValueFlag(a)) {
       var value = messageValueAfter(args, i);
       return { text: value, next: value === null ? i + 1 : i + 2 };  // CC 1 + ternary 1

   if (isJoinedShortMessage(a)) return { text: a.substring(2), next: i + 1 };

}
``

function commitMessageText(args, fileContents) {

#!/bin/bash

Important subtlety: `-m` branch FIRST: `/^-[a-zA-Z]*m$/` matches '-m'... and ALSO '-mF'? No wait: '-mF' ends with F — cluster-m regex needs to END with m: '-mF' doesn't match. Careful design of the extraction to keep CRAP ≤ 8 per helper with 100% coverage:

```js
/**
 * The message value carried by an -m/--message-style flag at args[i] —
 * the following token, or null when the flag is the last argument.
 */
function messageValueAfter(args, i) {
   return i + 1 < args.length ? args[i + 1] : null;  // CC 2
}

/**
 * File content registered for a -F/--file argument path (the caller reads
 * files; this module stays I/O-free) — null when unknown/empty.
 */
function fileContentFor(fileContents, path) {
   return (fileContents && fileContents[path]) ? fileContents[path] : null; // CC 3 (&& + ternary)
}
``

Wait original: `if (i + 1 < args.length && fileContents && fileContents[args[i + 1]]) parts.push(fileContents[args[i + 1]]);` — the i+1 bounds check is included. So fileFlagPart:

```js
function fileFlagPart(args, i, fileContents) {
   var content = i + 1 < args.length ? fileContentFor(fileContents, args[i + 1]) : null;
   return { text: content, next: i + 2 };  // CC: 1 + ternary 1 = 2
}
``

Crap counting: fileContentFor CC = ternary + && = 3. messageValueAfter CC 2.

isMessageValueFlag CC: `a === '-m' || a === '--message' || /^.../.test(a)` → CC 3.
isFileValueFlag CC 3.
isInlineMessageOption CC 1 (or 2 if I count `=== 0`... no decisions, CC 1).
isJoinedShortMessage: `a.indexOf('-m') === 0 && a.length > 2 && a.indexOf('--') !== 0` → CC 3.
isInlineFileOption CC 1.

commitMessagePartAt:

```js
function commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents) {
   var a = args[i];
   if (isMessageValueFlag(a)) {
       var value = messageValueAfter(args, i);
       return { text: value, next: value === null ? i + 1 : i + 2 };  // CC 1 + ternary 1
   }
   if (isInlineMessageOption(a)) return { text: a.substring('--message='.length), next: i + 1 };
   if (isJoinedShortMessage(a)) return { text: a.substring(2), next: i + 1 };
   if (isFileValueFlag(a)) return fileFlagPart(args, i, fileContents);
   if (isInlineFileOption(a)) return { text: fileContentFor(fileContents, a.substring('--file='.length)), next: i + 1 };
   return { text: null, next: i + 1 };
}
``

CC: 1 + 5 ifs + 1 ternary = 7. Under 8 ✓ (needs 100% coverage: each if both ways — my characterization matrix covers every one: message flag (yes via -m; no via others), inline message (yes --message=), joined (-mx), file flag (-F), inline file (--file=), default (token 'x')).

commitMessageText:

```js
function commitMessageText(args, fileContents) {
   var parts = [];
   var i = 0;
   while (i < args.length) {
       var part = commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents);
       if (part.text !== null) parts.push(part.text);
       i = part.next;

}
``

CC: 1 + while + if = 3. ✓

Equivalence audit vs original, case by case:
1. `-m`/`--message`/cluster with next: push args[i+1] (even ''), i+=2. Mine: value = args[i+1] (could be ''), text!==null → push, next i+2. ✓

3. `--message=X`: push X, i+=1. Mine: text X (could be '' for '--message=') → push '' (original pushes '' too), next i+1. ✓
4. joined -mX: push substring(2), i+=1. ✓
5. -F with content: original `if (i+1 < len && fileContents && fileContents[next])` push, i+=2 unconditionally. Mine: fileFlagPart: content = in-bounds ? fileContentFor(...) : null; text pushed iff non-null; next always i+2. ✓

  - in-bounds + no content → nothing, i+=2 ✓
  - out of bounds (-F at end) → nothing, i+=2 → loop ends ✓
6. `--file=f`: original `if (fileContents && fileContents[f]) parts.push(...)`; i+=1. Mine: text = fileContentFor (null-safe), next i+1. ✓
7. other tokens: skip i+=1. ✓

One more subtlety — ORDER of checks. Original order: (1) -m cluster... (2) --message= (3) joined -m (4) -F cluster (5) --file=. Mine keeps the same order. ✓

Could a token match BOTH isMessageValueFlag and isInlineMessageOption? '-m...' variants: '--message=' — does it match cluster regex? '^-[a-zA-Z]*m$' — '--message=' has '=', no. ✓ disjoint enough.

#!/bin/bash

/**

function commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents) {

1. `-m msg` → next token
2. `--message msg` → next token
3. `-cm`-style cluster (regex `/^-[a-zA-Z]*m$/`) → next token
4. `-m` at END of args (no next) → skip
5. `--message=msg` → inline
6. `-mMsg` joined → inline substring(2)
7. `-F file` with map content → file content, skips value (i+=2)
8. `-F file` WITHOUT map content → nothing pushed, still skips (i+=2)
9. `-F` at end → skip (i+=2)
10. `--file=file` with map → content
11. `--file=file` without map → nothing
12. unrelated tokens skipped
13. multiple parts joined with '\n'
14. empty args → ''
15. `--file=` empty path → nothing (fileContents['] undefined)
16. cluster `-abcF` → file flag with next as file
17. `-m ''` (empty next token) → pushes ''

Also check: how do the current tests load the module? `loadModule('js/common/gitPushGuard.js', makeRequire({}), {})` — and file_read global available (shim parity suite uses file_read directly — provided by the harness's global env? The test uses `file_read({path})` — the node harness provides file_* globals presumably).

Now the `-F` branch: `if (a === '-F' || a === '--file' || /^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/.test(a))`. NOTE: the regex `/^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/` also matches '--file'? No: '--file' = '-','file'... wait /^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/ — '--file' has chars - f i l e: after first '-', the rest '-file' contains '-', not in [a-zA-Z], so no match. OK.

Important subtlety: `-m` branch FIRST: `/^-[a-zA-Z]*m$/` matches '-m'... and ALSO '-mF'? No wait: '-mF' ends with F — cluster-m regex needs to END with m: '-mF' doesn't match. Cluster-F regex /^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/ matches '-mF'! So '-mF file.txt' → treated as -F cluster flag. Fun. I'll include that in tests.

Also '--message' exact → first branch (next token). Note: '--message' also... first condition `a === '-m' || a === '--message' || /^-[a-zA-Z]*m$/.test(a)`.

What about '-m' cluster regex matching '--'? No ('-' not in class).

Edge: '-mx' — cluster-m fails (ends x), --message= fails, joined: indexOf('-m')===0 ✓, length 3>2 ✓, indexOf('--')!==0 ✓ → pushed 'x'.

Edge: '--mx'? indexOf('-m') — '--mx'.indexOf('-m') = 1 ≠ 0 → not joined. Skipped entirely.

Edge: '-m=' — joined: substring(2) = '='.

Now the empty-string value edge: `['-m', ']` → parts.push(') → join('\n') = ''. Characterization: commitMessageText(['-m',']) === ''.

And what does commitMessageText([], ...) return? '' (join of empty). And commitMessageText(undefined)? `args.length` would throw — callers always pass arrays (extractSubcommand guarantees args: []). Not my concern; keep as is.

Now for `fileContents` truthiness: `{}` → fileContents truthy but lookup undefined → skip.

Careful design of the extraction to keep CRAP ≤ 8 per helper with 100% coverage:

```js
/**
 * The message value carried by an -m/--message-style flag at args[i] —
 * the following token, or null when the flag is the last argument.
 */
function messageValueAfter(args, i) {
   return i + 1 < args.length ? args[i + 1] : null;  // CC 2
}

/**
 * File content registered for a -F/--file argument path (the caller reads
 * files; this module stays I/O-free) — null when unknown/empty.
 */
function fileContentFor(fileContents, path) {
   return (fileContents && fileContents[path]) ? fileContents[path] : null; // CC 3 (&& + ternary)
}
``

Wait original: `if (i + 1 < args.length && fileContents && fileContents[args[i + 1]]) parts.push(fileContents[args[i + 1]]);` — the i+1 bounds check is included. So fileFlagPart:

```js
function fileFlagPart(args, i, fileContents) {
   var content = i + 1 < args.length ? fileContentFor(fileContents, args[i + 1]) : null;
   return { text: content, next: i + 2 };  // CC: 1 + ternary 1 = 2
}
``

Crap counting: fileContentFor CC = ternary + && = 3. messageValueAfter CC 2.

isMessageValueFlag CC: `a === '-m' || a === '--message' || /^.../.test(a)` → CC 3.
isFileValueFlag CC 3.
isInlineMessageOption CC 1 (or 2 if I count `=== 0`... no decisions, CC 1).
isJoinedShortMessage: `a.indexOf('-m') === 0 && a.length > 2 && a.indexOf('--') !== 0` → CC 3.
isInlineFileOption CC 1.

commitMessagePartAt:

```js
function commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents) {
   var a = args[i];
   if (isMessageValueFlag(a)) {
       var value = messageValueAfter(args, i);
       return { text: value, next: value === null ? i + 1 : i + 2 };  // CC 1 + ternary 1
   }
   if (isInlineMessageOption(a)) return { text: a.substring('--message='.length), next: i + 1 };
   if (isJoinedShortMessage(a)) return { text: a.substring(2), next: i + 1 };
   if (isFileValueFlag(a)) return fileFlagPart(args, i, fileContents);
   if (isInlineFileOption(a)) return { text: fileContentFor(fileContents, a.substring('--file='.length)), next: i + 1 };
   return { text: null, next: i + 1 };
}
``

CC: 1 + 5 ifs + 1 ternary = 7. Under 8 ✓ (needs 100% coverage: each if both ways — my characterization matrix covers every one: message flag (yes via -m; no via others), inline message (yes --message=), joined (-mx), file flag (-F), inline file (--file=), default (token 'x')).

commitMessageText:

```js
function commitMessageText(args, fileContents) {
   var parts = [];
   var i = 0;
   while (i < args.length) {
       var part = commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents);
       if (part.text !== null) parts.push(part.text);
       i = part.next;
   }
   return parts.join('\n');
}
``

CC: 1 + while + if = 3. ✓

Equivalence audit vs original, case by case:
1. `-m`/`--message`/cluster with next: push args[i+1] (even ''), i+=2. Mine: value = args[i+1] (could be ''), text!==null → push, next i+2. ✓
2. message flag at end (no next): original pushes nothing, i+=1. Mine: value null → text null → no push, next i+1. ✓
3. `--message=X`: push X, i+=1. Mine: text X (could be '' for '--message=') → push '' (original pushes '' too), next i+1. ✓
4. joined -mX: push substring(2), i+=1. ✓
5. -F with content: original `if (i+1 < len && fileContents && fileContents[next])` push, i+=2 unconditionally. Mine: fileFlagPart: content = in-bounds ? fileContentFor(...) : null; text pushed iff non-null; next always i+2. ✓ 
  - in-bounds + content → push content, i+=2 ✓
  - in-bounds + no content → nothing, i+=2 ✓
  - out of bounds (-F at end) → nothing, i+=2 → loop ends ✓
6. `--file=f`: original `if (fileContents && fileContents[f]) parts.push(...)`; i+=1. Mine: text = fileContentFor (null-safe), next i+1. ✓
7. other tokens: skip i+=1. ✓

One more subtlety — ORDER of checks. Original order: (1) -m cluster... (2) --message= (3) joined -m (4) -F cluster (5) --file=. Mine keeps the same order. ✓

Could a token match BOTH isMessageValueFlag and isInlineMessageOption? '-m...' variants: '--message=' — does it match cluster regex? '^-[a-zA-Z]*m$' — '--message=' has '=', no. ✓ disjoint enough.

Now — gitPushGuard exports: add commitMessagePartAt? The existing exports list all helpers. I'll export: isMessageValueFlag? Hmm — exporting every tiny predicate is noise; but for CRAP ≤ 8 each needs full coverage, which the characterization matrix gives INDIRECTLY through commitMessageText (coverage counts per line/function). crap4js computes per-function coverage from statements intersecting the method's line range — indirect coverage through commitMessageText's tests covers the helpers' statements as long as the helper code is EXECUTED. isMessageValueFlag true/false both covered by the matrix. So I don't strictly need direct tests of predicates, but a few direct assertions are cheap and pin each helper. Important subtlety: `-m` branch FIRST: `/^-[a-zA-Z]*m$/` matches '-m'... and ALSO '-mF'? No wait: '-mF' ends with F — cluster-m regex needs to END with m: '-mF' doesn't match. Cluster-F regex /^-[a-zA-Z]*F$/ matches '-mF'! So '-mF file.txt' → treated as -F cluster flag. Fun. I'll include that in tests.

```js
/**
 * The message value carried by an -m/--message-style flag at args[i] —
 * the following token, or null when the flag is the last argument.
 */
function messageValueAfter(args, i) {
   return i + 1 < args.length ? args[i + 1] : null;  // CC 2
}

/**
 * File content registered for a -F/--file argument path (the caller reads
 * files; this module stays I/O-free) — null when unknown/empty.
 */
function fileContentFor(fileContents, path) {
   return (fileContents && fileContents[path]) ? fileContents[path] : null; // CC 3 (&& + ternary)
}
``

Wait original: `if (i + 1 < args.length && fileContents && fileContents[args[i + 1]]) parts.push(fileContents[args[i + 1]]);` — the i+1 bounds check is included. So fileFlagPart:

   return { text: content, next: i + 2 };  // CC: 1 + ternary 1 = 2

``

isMessageValueFlag CC: `a === '-m' || a === '--message' || /^.../.test(a)` → CC 3.
isFileValueFlag CC 3.

commitMessagePartAt:

```js
function commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents) {
   var a = args[i];
   if (isMessageValueFlag(a)) {
       var value = messageValueAfter(args, i);
       return { text: value, next: value === null ? i + 1 : i + 2 };  // CC 1 + ternary 1

   if (isJoinedShortMessage(a)) return { text: a.substring(2), next: i + 1 };
   if (isFileValueFlag(a)) return fileFlagPart(args, i, fileContents);
   if (isInlineFileOption(a)) return { text: fileContentFor(fileContents, a.substring('--file='.length)), next: i + 1 };
   return { text: null, next: i + 1 };
}
``

CC: 1 + 5 ifs + 1 ternary = 7. Under 8 ✓ (needs 100% coverage: each if both ways — my characterization matrix covers every one: message flag (yes via -m; no via others), inline message (yes --message=), joined (-mx), file flag (-F), inline file (--file=), default (token 'x')).

commitMessageText:

```js
function commitMessageText(args, fileContents) {

       if (part.text !== null) parts.push(part.text);

}
``

function commitMessagePartAt(args, i, fileContents) {

Two characterization test failures against current code — my mock bug: `happyReworkCli(commands, currentBranch)` — for the mismatch test I passed currentBranch='bug/wrong' as the --show-current output AND used it in the ls-remote pattern — but after the forced checkout, `verifyReworkPushed(cmd, branchName='bug/PROJ-123')` probes ls-remote for 'bug/PROJ-123', which my mock doesn't answer (returns '' → branch doesn't exist → throw). Fix the mock: answer ls-remote for BOTH branches. Also the base-branch refusal test: currentBranch='develop' — checkout to 'bug/PROJ-123' FAILS silently in the mock (returns '' for git checkout — no throw!) → branchName stays 'develop' → refusal thrown... but the error says 'Branch was not successfully pushed to remote' — that means the refusal did NOT trigger?!

Wait — for the refusal test: expectedBranch='bug/PROJ-123', baseBranch='develop', currentBranch='develop' → mismatch → checkout 'bug/PROJ-123' → my happyReworkCli returns '' (no throw) → branchName stays 'develop' → `branchName === baseBranch` → should throw refusal...

But the error shows the test got past to verifyReworkPushed?? That means branchName !== 'develop'. Hmm — because happyReworkCli DOES throw? No... wait — the mismatch condition: `expectedBranch && currentBranch !== expectedBranch` — 'develop' !== 'bug/PROJ-123' → true → checkout branch → cmd('git checkout bug/PROJ-123') → happy mock returns '' → no error → branchName stays 'develop'... then `if (branchName && branchName === baseBranch)` → 'develop' === 'develop' → THROW refusal. But the test error says 'Branch was not successfully pushed to remote' — that's from verifyReworkPushed, meaning commitAndPush DIDN'T throw refusal.

OH WAIT — look at my mock: `happyReworkCli(commands, 'develop')`: `if (args.command.indexOf('git ls-remote --heads origin develop') === 0)` — the push happens... but refusal should have thrown before. Let me re-check: baseConfig() has `git: { baseBranch: 'develop' }`. pr_info: '**Branch**: `bug/PROJ-123` → `develop`' — the BASE parse: regex `\*\*Branch\*\*:\s*`[^`]+`\s*→\s*`([^`]+)` matches → baseBranch = 'develop'. currentBranch = 'develop' — hmm wait, but branchName = currentBranch = 'develop'... 

Hold on, actually let me re-check the checkout step. `cmd('git checkout bug/PROJ-123')` — happyReworkCli returns '' → no exception → `branchName = expectedBranch` = 'bug/PROJ-123'!!! The ORIGINAL code sets branchName = expectedBranch AFTER cmd() succeeds — regardless of output. So branchName = 'bug/PROJ-123', NOT 'develop'! The refusal doesn't fire; the flow continues to push 'bug/PROJ-123'.

So for the refusal path, the CHECKOUT must FAIL (throw) — like the existing test does ('git checkout bug/PROJ-123' throws → catch → branchName stays current). My refusal test needs a cli mock where checkout throws. Let me fix: use a custom mock for that test (checkout throws).

And the mismatch-success test: ls-remote must answer for 'bug/PROJ-123' (the final branchName). Fix happyReworkCli to answer ls-remote for a LIST of branches. Let me restructure: happyReworkCli(commands, branches[]) — branch --show-current → branches[0]; ls-remote for any of branches → sha.

Two characterization test failures against current code — my mock bug: `happyReworkCli(commands, currentBranch)` — for the mismatch test I passed currentBranch='bug/wrong' as the --show-current output AND used it in the ls-remote pattern — but after the forced checkout, `verifyReworkPushed(cmd, branchName='bug/PROJ-123')` probes ls-remote for 'bug/PROJ-123', which my mock doesn't answer (returns '' → branch doesn't exist → throw). Fix the mock: answer ls-remote for BOTH branches. Also the base-branch refusal test: currentBranch='develop' — checkout to 'bug/PROJ-123' FAILS silently in the mock (returns '' for git checkout — no throw!) → branchName stays 'develop' → refusal thrown... but the error says 'Branch was not successfully pushed to remote' — that means the refusal did NOT trigger?!

Wait — for the refusal test: expectedBranch='bug/PROJ-123', baseBranch='develop', currentBranch='develop' → mismatch → checkout 'bug/PROJ-123' → my happyReworkCli returns '' (no throw) → branchName stays 'develop' → `branchName === baseBranch` → should throw refusal...

But the error shows the test got past to verifyReworkPushed?? That means branchName !== 'develop'. Hmm — because happyReworkCli DOES throw? No... wait — the mismatch condition: `expectedBranch && currentBranch !== expectedBranch` — 'develop' !== 'bug/PROJ-123' → true → checkout branch → cmd('git checkout bug/PROJ-123') → happy mock returns '' → no error → branchName stays 'develop'... then `if (branchName && branchName === baseBranch)` → 'develop' === 'develop' → THROW refusal. But the test error says 'Branch was not successfully pushed to remote' — that's from verifyReworkPushed, meaning commitAndPush DIDN'T throw refusal.

OH WAIT — look at my mock: `happyReworkCli(commands, 'develop')`: `if (args.command.indexOf('git ls-remote --heads origin develop') === 0)` — the push happens... but refusal should have thrown before. Let me re-check: baseConfig() has `git: { baseBranch: 'develop' }`. pr_info: '**Branch**: `bug/PROJ-123` → `develop`' — the BASE parse: regex `\*\*Branch\*\*:\s*`[^`]+`\s*→\s*`([^`]+)` matches → baseBranch = 'develop'. currentBranch = 'develop' — hmm wait, but branchName = currentBranch = 'develop'... 

Hold on, actually let me re-check the checkout step. `cmd('git checkout bug/PROJ-123')` — happyReworkCli returns '' → no exception → `branchName = expectedBranch` = 'bug/PROJ-123'!!! The ORIGINAL code sets branchName = expectedBranch AFTER cmd() succeeds — regardless of output. So branchName = 'bug/PROJ-123', NOT 'develop'! The refusal doesn't fire; the flow continues to push 'bug/PROJ-123'.

So for the refusal path, the CHECKOUT must FAIL (throw) — like the existing test does ('git checkout bug/PROJ-123' throws → catch → branchName stays current). My refusal test needs a cli mock where checkout throws. Let me fix: use a custom mock for that test (checkout throws).

And the mismatch-success test: ls-remote must answer for 'bug/PROJ-123' (the final branchName). Fix happyReworkCli to answer ls-remote for a LIST of branches. Let me restructure: happyReworkCli(commands, branches[]) — branch --show-current → branches[0]; ls-remote for any of branches → sha.

Two mock bugs in my new tests: (1) `verifyReworkPushed` probes ls-remote for the FINAL branch name (post-checkout), my mock only answered for the pre-checkout one; (2) the refusal path needs the checkout to FAIL (current code sets `branchName = expectedBranch` after a successful `cmd()` regardless of output).
